mainTopic: The end of the story of איבות בר איהי's לחי (where a person sleeps sets his residence), and רב's ruling about an alley shared by a גוי and a Jew, with אביי and רב יוסף discussing its reason
overview: This amud finishes the story of איבות בר איהי, who lived in an alley and set up a לחי with שמואל's permission, even though רבי אלעזר had objected that a לחי needs an alley with several residences. After שמואל died, רב ענן knocked the לחי down, and איבות protested. The גמרא first concludes from this that שמואל never accepted רבי אלעזר's objection. It then rejects that proof: a חזן slept in a synagogue on that alley, so it really had more than one residence. איבות misunderstood because he held that where a person eats determines his residence, while שמואל holds that where he sleeps determines it. Next, רב rules that in an alley with a גוי on one side and a Jew on the other, the Jews may not make an עירוב through windows to permit carrying through the doors into the alley. אביי asks רב יוסף whether this applies to a חצר too, and explains that he might have thought רב's reason applies only to a מבוי. רב יוסף challenges this, asking why רב would need two rulings. אביי begins to answer that both are needed, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב ענן knocks down the לחי and איבות protests
steps.stepSummary: After שמואל's death, רב ענן threw down the לחי of איבות בר איהי's alley. איבות complained that he had relied on שמואל's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן came and threw it down. איבות said: 'The alley I have been living in, relying on the ruling of Master שמואל, shall רב ענן בר רב come and throw it away from me?!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. רב ענן tore down the לחי, and איבות בר איהי protested that he had been relying on שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ענן acted because he understood that a single resident cannot permit an alley with a לחי, which is רבי אלעזר's objection. איבות protests because this לחי stood the whole time שמואל was alive. The story sets up the question of what שמואל really held.

keyTerms.meaning: I live / I have been living
in the name of (relying on) Master שמואל

phrases.english: Rav Anan came and threw it (the side post) down.
He (Ivut) said: The alley in which I have been living
and I have been acting on the ruling of Master Shmuel,

phrases.aramaic: נֵיתֵי רַב עָנָן בַּר רַב נִישְׁדְּיֵיהּ מִן?!
phrases.english: shall Rav Anan bar Rav come and throw it away from me?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of איבות בר איהי on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Historical fact: the לחי stood during שמואל's lifetime and was removed only afterward by רב ענן.

steps.title: Inference that שמואל never accepted the objection
steps.stepSummary: Since the לחי stood all of שמואל's life, the גמרא concludes that he did not accept רבי אלעזר's objection.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that he did not accept it from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the story. שמואל did not accept רבי אלעזר's objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמואל had agreed with רבי אלעזר, he would have taken the לחי down himself. The fact that only רב ענן removed it after שמואל died seems to prove that שמואל stood by his original ruling.

phrases.english: Learn from this that he (Shmuel) did not accept it (the objection) from him (Rabbi Elazar).
phrases.notes: We can tell because the לחי stayed up the whole time שמואל was alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the story in step 1
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל did not retract in the face of רבי אלעזר's objection
steps.raayaSupportSource: The לחי remained standing throughout שמואל's lifetime

steps.title: Rejection: a synagogue attendant slept there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. שמואל may have accepted the objection, because this alley had a חזן who slept in the synagogue there, so it had more than one residence.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, I can tell you that he did accept it from him. Here there was a synagogue attendant who would eat bread in his own house and come and sleep in the synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 2. It shows that the story does not prove שמואל disagreed with רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This alley was special: a חזן slept in the בית כנסת that opened onto it. So איבות was not really alone in the alley, and the לחי was valid even according to רבי אלעזר. שמואל's permission therefore fits with accepting the objection.

keyTerms.meaning: actually, I can tell you (opens a rejection)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חזן lived permanently in the synagogue. He ate at home elsewhere and only slept in the synagogue. That detail is exactly what the next step turns on.

phrases.english: Actually, I can tell you he did accept it from him,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is pushing back on that proof.

phrases.english: and here, it was a synagogue attendant
who would eat bread in his own house
and would come and sleep in the synagogue.
phrases.notes: The synagogue opened onto this alley.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the conclusion that שמואל did not accept רבי אלעזר's objection
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed איבות was the alley's only resident. In fact a חזן slept there, so the לחי was valid even according to רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: Eating place versus sleeping place determines residence
steps.stepSummary: איבות held that where one eats determines residence, so he thought he lived alone. שמואל holds that where one sleeps determines residence, so the חזן counted as a resident.
steps.simpleTranslation: And איבות בר איהי held: the place of bread determines residence. And שמואל follows his own reasoning, for he said: the place of sleeping determines residence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how איבות misunderstood שמואל's permission. It also shows that שמואל was being consistent with his own known view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איבות thought the חזן did not count, because he ate elsewhere. So איבות believed שמואל permitted a לחי for a lone resident. Really, שמואל holds that the sleeping place is a person's residence, so the alley had two residences and was validly permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: the place where one eats bread determines residence
the place where one sleeps determines residence

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל holds מקום לינה גרים: residence for עירוב purposes is set by where a person sleeps, not where he eats. This explains why the לחי was valid, and why שמואל could have accepted רבי אלעזר's objection.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question of whether eating or sleeping defines a person's dwelling has wide effects in הלכות עירובין, for example in deciding who must join an עירוב.

phrases.english: And Ivut bar Ihi held:
the place of (eating) bread determines residence.
phrases.notes: So he thought the חזן did not count, and that he himself lived alone.

phrases.english: But Shmuel follows his own reasoning, for he said:
the place of sleeping determines residence.
phrases.notes: So the חזן counted as a resident of the alley.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַיְבוּת בַּר אִיהִי סָבַר: מְקוֹם פִּיתָּא גָּרֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection in step 3 by explaining איבות's misunderstanding
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different underlying principles: eating place versus sleeping place
steps.terutzHavaAmina: איבות thought שמואל allowed a לחי for a lone resident, since the חזן ate elsewhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל counts the sleeping place, so the חזן made the alley a multi-residence alley. The permission is consistent with accepting רבי אלעזר's objection.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The story does not prove שמואל rejected רבי אלעזר. שמואל holds מקום לינה גרים.

steps.title: רב: an alley shared by a gentile and a Jew cannot be permitted through windows
steps.stepSummary: רב rules about an alley with a גוי on one side and a Jew on the other. The Jewish residents may not make an עירוב through windows in order to permit carrying through the doors into the alley.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: An alley with a גוי on one side and a Jew on the other, one may not make an עירוב for it through windows in order to permit it through doors to the alley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ruling from רב. It concerns an alley shared with a גוי, where the Jew's house connects to other Jewish homes only through windows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other Jewish houses open into the public domain and connect to this house only by windows. רב says that an עירוב made through those windows does not let those residents carry through this house's doors into the alley. The reason behind רב's ruling is not stated here. Steps 6-10 begin to explore its scope and reason, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
An alley, one side of which is occupied by a gentile
and one side of which is occupied by a Jew,
phrases.notes: The Jew's house connects to other Jewish homes only by windows.

phrases.english: one may not make an eiruv for it through the windows
in order to permit it through the doors to the alley.
phrases.notes: The windows do not make the other Jews residents of the alley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic, unrelated to the story of איבות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In an alley shared by a גוי and a Jew, an עירוב through windows with other Jewish houses does not permit carrying through the doors into the alley.

steps.title: אביי asks whether רב's ruling also applies to a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף whether רב's ruling about a גוי and a Jew applies even in a חצר, and not only in a מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Did רב say this even about a courtyard?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks רב יוסף how wide רב's ruling from Step 5 is. Does it work only in a מבוי (alley), or also in a חצר (courtyard)?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's ruling was said about a מבוי. Here a גוי lives on one side and a Jew on the other, and the Jews may not make an עירוב through windows. אביי wants to know whether the same rule applies when this setup happens inside a חצר.

keyTerms.meaning: A courtyard shared by several houses
An alley into which several courtyards open

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
Did Rav say this even about a courtyard?
phrases.notes: It means the same case of a גוי on one side and a Jew on the other, but inside a courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far רב's ruling from Step 5 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רב's ruling also apply to a חצר, or only to a מבוי?

steps.title: רב יוסף answers yes, since it is the same principle
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers yes. Even if רב had not said it outright, it would make no difference, because the logic is the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. And even if he had not said it, what difference would it make?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that רב's ruling applies to a חצר too. He adds that the question hardly matters, because the reasoning is obviously identical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumes that רב's reason has nothing to do with the special nature of a מבוי. So whatever applies in a מבוי automatically applies in a חצר. The words 'what difference would it make?' invite אביי to show why the question really matters.

keyTerms.meaning: For if he had not said it, what (difference would it make)?

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
for if he had not said it, what difference would it make?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, דְּאִי לָא אָמַר מַאי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the ruling applies to a חצר too, since it is the same principle.

steps.title: אביי explains he might have read רב's reason as limited to alleys
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains why his question matters. He might have thought רב's reason was that a מבוי can only be permitted with a לחי or קורה if houses and courtyards open into it. That reason belongs only to a מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: I would have said that רב's reason is because he holds: an alley is not permitted through a side post and a crossbeam unless houses and courtyards open into it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב יוסף's 'what difference would it make?' He shows there is another possible reason for רב's ruling, and that reason would apply only to a מבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that a מבוי only counts as a real alley if houses and courtyards open into it. If רב's ruling were based on that rule, it would apply only to a מבוי, not to a חצר. That is why אביי needed to ask whether רב said it about a חצר too.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a first idea that may turn out wrong)
A side post at the entrance of an alley, which permits carrying inside it
A crossbeam over the entrance of an alley, which also permits carrying inside it
Houses and courtyards that open into the alley

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT a new ruling. אביי is only explaining what he might have thought, which shows why his question was worth asking.

phrases.english: I would have said
that Rav's reason is because he holds:
an alley is not permitted through a side post and crossbeam

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ בָּתִּים וַחֲצֵירוֹת פְּתוּחִין לְתוֹכוֹ.
phrases.english: unless there are houses and courtyards opening into it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא טַעְמָא דְּרַב מִשּׁוּם דְּקָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's 'what difference would it make?' by offering a reason that applies only to a מבוי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question matters because רב's reason might have been a rule that applies only to a מבוי.

steps.title: Why would רב need two rulings
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges אביי's idea. If רב's reason were the 'houses and courtyards' rule, why would רב need a second ruling? He had already taught that rule separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need two rulings?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks אביי's possible reading of רב. If that reading were right, רב's ruling about the גוי would just repeat something רב already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב already stated elsewhere that a מבוי needs houses and courtyards opening into it. If the ruling about the גוי were based on that same idea, it would add nothing new. The גמרא assumes a teacher does not repeat himself without a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need two (statements)? The question asks why something seems to be said twice.

phrases.english: And why do I need two rulings?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason אביי suggested in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's suggestion that רב's reason is the rule that a מבוי needs houses and courtyards opening into it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were the reason, רב's ruling about the גוי would just repeat his earlier rule, and that would be pointless.

steps.title: Both rulings are needed: the answer begins
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins to answer that both rulings are necessary. 'If we only had that one ruling...' The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. For if we only had that ruling...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts to answer רב יוסף's challenge by saying that both rulings are needed. This line is only the setup. The full explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word צריכא signals that the גמרא will show what each ruling teaches that the other one could not. Here it begins: 'if we learned it only from that one...' It will then explain what mistake we could have made with just one ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary. Both statements are needed, because each teaches something the other does not.
For if (we learned it only) from that one

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is cut off on purpose at the end of the amud. Do not look for the full answer here; it continues in the next section.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
for if we learned it only from that one —
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to answer the challenge in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that both statements are needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like the second ruling only repeated the first.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ruling teaches something unique. The details are explained on the next amud.
